skill.name: indeed-global-job-scraper-with-company-salary-reports
skill.description: Search public Indeed jobs through an Apify Actor with filters for country, location, company, salary, and experience. Retrieve JSON results with job details and optional company reports.
skill.summary: Retrieve public Indeed job listings and company salary reports through Apify.
skill.author: bolvein-firex

security_audit.summary: All 79 static findings are false positives involving documentation syntax, fixed resource paths, explicit input reads, or documented Apify authentication and requests. The external Actor implementation is not included, so its runtime behavior was not verified.

content.user_title: Extract Indeed Jobs and Company Salary Reports
content.value_statement: Comparing public job postings and employer salary information requires repeated searches. This skill submits filtered Indeed searches to Apify and retrieves structured results for review.
actual_capabilities: Configure searches across 62 country options using keywords, locations, employer names, or Indeed URLs.
Apply filters for employment type, workplace, posting date, experience, education, and minimum salary.
Request job details, structured salary fields, employer ratings, and optional company reports through the external Actor.
Configure location shards, date windows, deduplication, and global or per-search item limits.
Run synchronous requests with the included Node.js runner using a JSON file or inline input.
Follow documented curl examples to start asynchronous runs and retrieve dataset results.
limitations: Requires an Apify token, network access, and billable Actor usage. The Node.js runner requires Node 18 or later.
The external Actor implementation is not bundled. Country coverage and returned fields depend on Indeed and the remote service.
Synchronous calls wait up to 300 seconds. The asynchronous example checks status once, so verify completion before downloading results.
The bundled runner outputs JSON only. Private data access and automated job applications are outside scope.

use_cases.title: Compare Public Openings
use_cases.description: Collect a small set of recent roles with location, workplace, salary, and employer information for manual comparison.

use_cases.title: Research Employer Compensation
use_cases.description: Retrieve public salary fields and optional company reports to compare advertised compensation while preserving currency and pay-period context.

use_cases.title: Review Regional Hiring
use_cases.description: Configure searches across selected cities and date windows with deduplication and explicit item limits for repeatable hiring research.

prompt_templates.title: Find Recent Jobs
prompt_templates.prompt: Find up to 25 public Indeed [role] jobs in [city], [country], posted within seven days. Confirm Apify costs before running. Summarize available salaries.

prompt_templates.title: Filter a Role Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Find up to 25 remote [role] jobs in [country] with [experience] experience and minimum yearly salary [amount]. Confirm filters and costs before running.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Employer Reports
prompt_templates.prompt: Search public Indeed jobs for [company] in [country]. Enable company reports and cap results at 25. Confirm costs first. Distinguish posting salaries from employer averages.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Regional Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare searches for [role] across [cities] in [country]. Enable date sharding and deduplication. Set maxItems to 100. Confirm costs. Verify asynchronous completion before retrieval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate bounded searches across locations.

output_examples.input: Describe the output of a limited search for recent account executive roles in Austin.
output: Illustrative output layout, not live search results.
Job comparison: title, employer, location, workplace, posting date, salary range, currency, and Indeed link.
Salary details are shown only when returned by the source.

output_examples.input: Describe a company salary report accompanying public job results.
output: Illustrative report layout, not live employer data.
Employer overview: rating, review count, industry, size, and available company details.
Compensation section: available salary averages by title, separate from individual posting salaries.
Unavailable fields remain unspecified rather than estimated.

best_practices: Start with maxItems set to 25, review Actor pricing, and confirm the intended Actor before authorizing a run.
Keep APIFY_TOKEN outside prompts and shared files. Send only public search inputs, without cookies, sessions, or private account data.
Verify run completion, inspect missing fields, and compare salaries using matching currencies and pay periods.
anti_patterns: Launching broad searches without item limits or reviewing the account charges.
Treating missing salaries as zero or comparing different currencies and pay periods without normalization.
Using collected contacts for spam, harassment, unlawful discrimination, or access to private data.

faq.question: Does this skill run without Apify?
faq.answer: No. It calls a hosted Apify Actor and requires APIFY_TOKEN. The local runner requires Node 18 or later.

faq.question: Is running a search free?
faq.answer: Apify bills Actor usage to your account. Check the current pricing and set an item limit before running.

faq.question: Which countries and filters are supported?
faq.answer: The input schema lists 62 countries. Filters include location, employer, job type, workplace, date, experience, education, and salary.

faq.question: Are salaries and company details always available?
faq.answer: No. Availability depends on source data and selected options. Company reports require additional requests, and sponsored flags are best effort.

faq.question: Can the runner export CSV?
faq.answer: The included runner prints JSON. CSV requires a separate conversion step or an export option outside this runner.

faq.question: How should large runs be handled?
faq.answer: Use the documented asynchronous endpoint. Check status until the run succeeds, then retrieve its dataset. The example checks status only once.
